readThisFirst: Enabling a preset does not make a cluster compliant with HIPAA, SOC 2, PCI DSS or anything else.
The mapping from these controls to any regulation has not been reviewed by anyone qualified.

ControlsMet being True means one thing: every check this operator performs passed the last time it ran. It does not mean your cluster is compliant, secure, or audit-ready. Do not present it to an auditor as proof of compliance.
pgaudit does not record an escalated session's reads and writes. Read the emergency access section before anyone uses it.

controls.evidence: pgaudit is loaded and logs read,write,ddl,role
TLS is on and connections without it are refused; the server certificate is generated by the image, not issued by a certificate authority, so clients cannot verify the server
passwords are stored as scram-sha-256 and no network connection rule skips the password
3 pod(s) each shipped within 15m0s of the check
no lifecycle rule expires audit logs before the 2190 days expected; objects are not protected from deletion, as the bucket has no object lock
the policy is in place and a pod with none of the allowed labels was refused (timeout)
backups are on, encrypted, healthy, and a restore test has passed
3 instances, with a ready primary and replication healthy

items: That the audit log cannot be altered.

warning.title: WARNING: while you are escalated, your statements and their values are logged in clear text
statements: pgaudit does not record an escalated session's reads and writes.
While escalated, the server writes every statement you run to its log, and it writes the values you bind to a statement's parameters there too, in clear text.
This happens whatever the cluster's audit settings say: logParameters: false does not stop it.
If you are using emergency access as part of an audit, your auditors will be able to read every value you used.
warning.record: These are the requests that exist now. A request that was deleted leaves nothing here. The server log, and the Kubernetes API server's audit log if you keep one, hold the rest of the record.
